description: Indefinite-integral (អាំងតេក្រាលមិនកំណត់) foundational drills: verifying a given antiderivative F(x) matches f(x), power-rule sums of monomials/negative powers, trig-power identity integrals (tan^2, cot^2), exponential/trig basic antiderivatives, and u-substitution forms (u'u^n, u'/u=ln|u|, u'e^u, linear-argument 1/(ax+b)).

source.description: Cambodian BAC II grade-12 math exercise compendium (Start Up Community), Lesson 8: អាំងតេក្រាលមិនកំណត់ (Indefinite Integrals), Section 1: power/basic techniques — exercises only, no worked solutions
source.extracted_by: manual OCR/transcription from scanned textbook (Claude Code), 2026-08-28

exercises.technique: Verify F'(x)=f(x) by differentiating the given antiderivative and checking it matches
antiderivative_power_rule: \int x^n dx = x^{n+1}/(n+1)+C applied to polynomial/negative-power/root sums
antiderivative_reciprocal + power_rule: split fraction into individual power terms, using \int1/x\,dx=\ln|x|

exercises.prompt_latex: \int(e^x-1)\,dx;\ \int(x+2e^x)\,dx;\ \int(e^x-2)/3\,dx;\ \int(x^2-10e^x+e^2)\,dx;\ \int(8e^x-6x)/4\,dx;\ \int(3x^2-xe^x+1)/x\,dx;\ \int(x+\cos x)\,dx;\ \int(x^2-2\sin x)\,dx;\ \int(2\cos x-3\sin x)\,dx;\ \int(\tfrac12\cos x-x+e^x/2)\,dx;\ \int(\sin x/2+2/x-1/2)\,dx;\ \int(e^x-4\cos x)/3\,dx
exercises.technique: antiderivative_exponential + antiderivative_trig, combined with power rule for mixed sums
antiderivative_trig_sec: rewrite tan^2x=1/\cos^2x-1, cot^2x=1/\sin^2x-1 (Pythagorean identity) before integrating
u_substitution: \int u'u^n\,dx=u^{n+1}/(n+1)+C, recognizing u' as a scalar multiple of the outer derivative

exercises.prompt_latex: \int(1/x)\ln x\,dx;\ \int3(\ln x)^3/(2x)\,dx;\ \int(\ln x-1)/x\,dx;\ \int(3+2\ln x)^2/x\,dx;\ \int4\cos x\sin x\,dx;\ \int\sin x\cos^3x\,dx;\ \int2\sin x(1-\cos x)^7\,dx;\ \int\cos x/\sin^9x\,dx
exercises.technique: u_substitution with u=\ln x or u=\sin x/\cos x: \int u'/u\,dx=\ln|u|, \int u'u^n\,dx=u^{n+1}/(n+1)
linear_argument_rule and u_substitution: \int1/(ax+b)\,dx=\ln|ax+b|/a, and recognizing u'/\sqrt u or u'/u^2 forms
